lesson: In overage_charge, prorate the included quota by calendar day and round UP to the next whole unit using ceil, rejecting truncation.
why: Truncating creates rounding artifacts that unfairly bill the customer, whereas fractional units must count in the customer's favor.
quote: The fractional unit counts in the customer's favor; truncating is how you bill someone over a rounding artifact.

lesson: In overage_charge, bill overages in 50-unit blocks rounded UP at plan['block_fee'] per block rather than billing per unit.
why: Finance reconciles revenue in whole blocks, and per-unit billing made reconciliation impossible.
quote: finance reconciles in whole blocks and per-unit line items made that impossible last quarter.

lesson: Do not add a waiver or threshold for small overages in overage_charge; even a single unit of overage must bill a full block.
why: Quotas were priced without waivers, and offering free units causes revenue leakage.
quote: any overage bills at least one block — free units are revenue leakage and the plan quotas were priced assuming none.

lesson: Keep the ValueError validation in overage_charge for any day_of_month outside the range 1..days_in_month.
why: This parameter validation has actively prevented and caught caller bugs in practice.
quote: keep the ValueError for a day outside 1..days_in_month, that guard has caught real caller bugs.

lesson: When calculating billable overage, apply a monthly grace allowance of 25 units before block rounding (`billable = max(0, overage - 25)`), superseding the previous no-free-units rule, and then round up into 50-unit blocks. Proration remains rounded up with ceil, and partial blocks bill as full blocks at `plan['block_fee']`.
why: Accidental small overruns were billing full blocks and requiring manual support credits that eroded more margin than the strict policy protected.
quote: every account gets a grace allowance of 25 overage units per month, and it applies BEFORE the block rounding.
